title: The Long Weekend
premise: The calendar on the kitchen wall has run out of days and kept going. Saturday appears nine times in a row, in the same confident handwriting, and somebody has been dutifully crossing each one off.
visual: Bright ordinary kitchen, mid-morning, coffee made. A wall calendar where the week reads MON TUE WED SATURDAY SATURDAY SATURDAY SATURDAY SATURDAY SATURDAY — the grid stretched to fit them all, printed not scrawled. Six are crossed off in red pen. A hand holds the pen over the seventh. Groceries on the counter for one more day than anyone needs.
characterLean: Nobody's sister. This is a house where somebody lives alone and is coping beautifully.
notes: Seed only — still prompt not locked. The calendar must look professionally printed, not hand-altered — the repetition is the publisher's error, not a joke somebody made. Daylight, tidy house, no dread props. Do not put a clock in frame and do not use 3:44. Sibling in spirit to Fig. 4: the authority of a printed thing that is wrong.
